text:
alex: Quick retrospective on the slice sundown gating — realized we need clearer rollback triggers and concrete metrics to pass the gate.

mira: Agreed. Canary showed ~8% token cost spike but p99 latency stayed fine. however error rate for three tenants rose ~2-3%.

devon: Any idea why cost jumped? Could be batching config change or quantization fallback churn.

alex: Hypothesis: routing fallback to medium-quant caused repeated warm-starts. saw logs with repeated model loads flagged as "hotload: 12x/min" during the window.

ryan: I saw the same. Suggest adding a token-cost budget for the canary and an automatic scale-down / rollback when exceeded.

mira: Also we should enforce per-tenant traffic shaping during sundown so noisy tenants can't blow past budgets.

devon: Proposed hard gate: block rollout if p99 latency > 80ms OR error_rate_delta > 1.5x for any monitored tenant during the canary window.

alex: +1. Also require stability across two consecutive canary windows (we're using 6h windows) before a full rollout.

ryan: Who will own the canary dashboard? I can add panels: p99 latency, evicted_sessions, model_loads/min, token_cost_rate, per-tenant error delta.

mira: Can we automate rollback via release manager? e.g. release-bot should trigger rollback when token budget or gates are violated.

devon: Adding the snippet to release playbook for rollback automation:

```
release-bot rollback --tag vSUNDOWN-rc1 --reason "token_budget_exceeded"
```

alex: Action items: ryan -> dashboard, devon -> update playbook with auto-rollback, mira -> update runbook with per-tenant thresholds and traffic-shaping knobs. I'll schedule a 30m check-in after next canary window.

ryan: noted, will post dashboard link here when ready :soon: .

release-bot: Canary started for sundown/vSUNDOWN-rc1 at 2025-12-12T08:00Z

mira: Thanks — reminder to include the synthetic prompt set that stresses long-form contexts, last canary missed those and we didn't catch kv-cache pressure.
